title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: makers can build declarative agents with flexible layouts and rich UX components
summary: Hold: the page incorrectly reports that User access has no documented automation. Microsoft documents a preview Graph route that applies the all-users or no-users setting through Tenant Configuration Management. The roadmap facts and printed control paths are supported.

claims.claim: An agent can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. ... In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The general block control restricts access to the selected agent across the organisation.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. ... Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: User access is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for the User access control.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api null with kind graph, call 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Add to the note: 'Preview TCM automation supports All users or No users: set mode to applyOnce and supply a baseline resource with resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion 1, and properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory set to everyone or noOne. Specific-user/group selection is not documented in this resource. applyOnce requires delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for the calling app, delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for the TCM service principal, and AI Administrator for the signed-in user.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-authentication-setup. The operation reference states that an active applyOnce monitor applies the baseline in a background job, then becomes inactive.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: User access controls which organisation members access and install agents and plugins.
claims.quote: Use User access to control how members of your organization access and install agents and plugins.

claims.claim: The existing User access setting defaults to All users.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agents affects only their availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Block and User access are agent-access controls rather than separate layout or component switches.
claims.quote: User access - Control which users or groups can interact with AI agents and plugins, aligning access with organizational roles and permissions.
